title: Time

segments.voice: Yesterday, money: a fine servant, a demanding master. Your line was money is a servant. Today, the one thing no paycheck buys more of.
screen: `MONEY IS A SERVANT.` → `WHAT NO PAYCHECK BUYS.`

segments.voice: A phone counts time without a sound, which may be why a whole evening can slip away without one. An old wall clock does it out loud: every second, a click. The letter to the Ephesians has a phrase for getting some of those clicks back: “Redeeming the time, because the days are evil.” Redeem, as in buy back, the way someone pays to get a thing out of a pawnshop. So what does it cost to buy back an hour?
screen: `TIME, WITHOUT A SOUND.` → `REDEEMING THE TIME.` → `WHAT DOES AN HOUR COST?`

segments.voice: Here's the whole sentence: “See then that ye walk circumspectly, not as fools, but as wise, Redeeming the time, because the days are evil.” Circumspectly means looking around as you walk, eyes open. The days are evil isn't a reason to panic; it's a reason not to drift. Time doesn't buy itself back. A psalm asks for the skill: “So teach us to number our days, that we may apply our hearts unto wisdom.” Counting days isn't gloomy. It makes them audible, the way a ticking clock makes a minute something you can hear. And Ecclesiastes keeps this from turning into frantic busyness: “To every thing there is a season, and a time to every purpose under the heaven.” A time to work, and a time to sit on a porch doing nothing much. So redeeming the time doesn't mean filling every minute. It means paying for some of them on purpose, with attention, and handing them to what lasts: prayer, scripture, a visit to someone lonely, worship with others, a long walk. Christians spend that hour in different ways. The price is the same for everyone: something else doesn't get it.
screen: `WALK CIRCUMSPECTLY, EYES OPEN.` · `TEACH US TO NUMBER OUR DAYS.` · `A SEASON FOR EVERY THING.` · `PAID FOR WITH ATTENTION.` · then, large: `REDEEM THE TIME.`

segments.voice: Find one steady sound near you: a clock, a fan, the hum of a fridge, or your own breath if the room is quiet. Listen to it for the whole sit, and let each beat be one moment you are actually there for. Before you finish, choose one hour this week to give to something that lasts.
Time. The days you're given, numbered and not endless, some of them bought back on purpose.
For the road: redeem the time, one chosen hour at a time. That's day 1726.
